headline: Westward bound for Dakota
summary: Roosevelt sets out for the West on his hunting trip. Henry H. Gorringe, who had first proposed it, drops out at the last moment. Roosevelt writes Bamie to tell her he is leaving for Dakota.

events.detail: Leaves New York City for a hunt in Dakota Territory
Henry H. Gorringe withdraws from the trip at the last minute
Writes Bamie that he is leaving on his Dakota hunt

letters.topic: Announces his departure for a Dakota hunting trip

tr_quotes.text: Today I leave for a hunting trip in Dakotah.

headline: In Chicago, in high spirits
summary: Roosevelt reaches Chicago and writes his mother that he feels full of fight.

events.detail: Arrives in Chicago on the way west

letters.topic: Reports he is feeling vigorous on the trip west

headline: Rolling west toward the Badlands
summary: Roosevelt is on the rails, heading for the Dakota Badlands.

events.detail: Traveling by train toward the Badlands

headline: Boarding the St. Paul Express
summary: Roosevelt switches trains to the St. Paul Express for the run west.

events.detail: Transfers to the St. Paul Express

headline: A 2 a.m. arrival in Little Missouri
summary: Roosevelt steps off the train at Little Missouri in Dakota Territory and rouses the owner of the Pyramid Park Hotel at two in the morning. He is given a bed in a fourteen-bed bunk room.

events.detail: Arrives at Little Missouri, Dakota Territory
Wakes the Pyramid Park Hotel's owner and takes a bed in a shared 14-bed room

uncertain: Most accounts place this arrival in the small hours of September 8, 1883; the record logs it under September 7.

headline: Joe Ferris signs on as guide
summary: Roosevelt hires 25-year-old Joe Ferris to guide him. Buffalo have been hunted hard in the Dakotas lately. They overnight at the Maltese Cross Ranch, which Sylvane Ferris, 24, runs with Bill Merrifield, 28; all three men came from Canada. Roosevelt also writes his mother.

events.detail: Hires Joe Ferris as his hunting guide
Puts up overnight at the Maltese Cross Ranch

letters.topic: Letter from Dakota; contents not described

headline: A mare named Nell and the Lang cabin
summary: Roosevelt buys a mare called Nell from Ferris, then rides 45 miles south to the cabin of Scotsman Gregor Lang and his son Lincoln, 16. Lang, sent by an English firm to scout cattle country, talks with Roosevelt past midnight about the region and the cattle trade.

events.detail: Buys a mare named Nell from Ferris
Rides about 45 miles south to the Lang cabin
Talks until midnight with Gregor Lang about the area's history and the cattle business

uncertain: The record says only 'Ferris', so which Ferris sold the mare is unclear.

headline: A missed buck in the rain
summary: Up at six on a soaking day, Roosevelt hunts with Joe Ferris. Ferris drops a blacktail buck at long range after Roosevelt misses it, to his own annoyance. That night Roosevelt again talks cattle with Gregor Lang late, while Ferris sleeps.

events.detail: Hunts in heavy rain; misses a blacktail buck that Ferris then kills
Late-night talk with Gregor Lang about ranching

headline: Mud and an empty game bag
summary: Roosevelt and Ferris hunt the whole day in the rain, bag nothing, and come back caked in mud. While Ferris sleeps, Roosevelt and Gregor Lang talk cattle, America and politics.

events.detail: Full day of hunting in the rain without success
Evening talk with Gregor Lang on cattle, America and politics

headline: More rain, more hunting
summary: Another wet day: Roosevelt hunts from morning to night and then talks late into the evening, just as before.

events.detail: Hunts all day in the rain
Talks late at the Lang cabin

headline: Cree riders in the rain
summary: Rain again. Roosevelt's party spots a band of wandering Cree, but otherwise the day repeats the last two.

events.detail: Another day of hunting in the rain
Sees a roving party of Cree Indians

headline: A wounded buffalo and a bloody brow
summary: Roosevelt hits a buffalo too far back and it gets away. In the chase the animal charges, his pony knocks his rifle into his head, and he bleeds from the cut. That night the horses bolt. Ferris hears him exclaim he is having fun.

events.detail: Wounds a buffalo that escapes after a chase and a charge
Cut on the head when his own rifle is driven into it
Sleeps in the open; the spooked horses run off in the night

tr_quotes.text: By godfrey, but this is fun!

headline: Rain in his eyes
summary: In cold rain, Roosevelt gets a shot but misses with water streaming into his eyes, and spends another drenched night outdoors.

events.detail: Misses a shot in the cold rain
Another night out in the rain

headline: Hard luck, and a choice to invest
summary: On a hot day Roosevelt tumbles down a cliff, is thrown from his horse, and nearly loses the horse to quicksand. After two days on biscuits and rainwater, he resolves to put money into the Badlands, and talks late with Gregor Lang again.

events.detail: Falls down a cliff and is thrown from his horse
His horse nearly founders in quicksand
Resolves to put money into a Badlands cattle venture
Returns to the Lang cabin with Ferris

headline: Hunting in the rain
summary: More rain, and more hunting for Roosevelt.

headline: A $14,000 stake in cattle
summary: With Sylvane Ferris and Bill Merrifield at the Lang cabin, Roosevelt hands them a $14,000 check to run his stock and purchase 450 cattle. The sum tops his entire income for the year, $13,920.

events.detail: Gives Sylvane Ferris and Merrifield $14,000 to buy and manage 450 cattle for him

headline: Drawing up a ranch contract
summary: At the Lang cabin Roosevelt writes out a ranch contract. Ferris and Merrifield head to Minnesota to be released by their employers, Wadsworth and Halley, so they can partner with him.

events.detail: Ferris and Merrifield go to Minnesota to leave the employ of Wadsworth and Halley

uncertain: The record says only 'Ferris'; Sylvane is assumed, since he managed the Maltese Cross with Merrifield.

headline: His buffalo at last
summary: Riding into Montana with Joe Ferris, Roosevelt finally brings down a bison bull. He celebrates with a whooping dance and hands Ferris $100 then and there.

events.detail: Celebrates and pays Ferris $100 on the spot

uncertain: The record describes the celebration as an 'Indian war dance'.

headline: Skinning the bull, riding back
summary: Roosevelt skins the bison he shot the previous day and then rides back to Little Missouri.

events.detail: Rides out and skins the bison

headline: At the Maltese Cross
summary: Roosevelt is at the Maltese Cross, the cabin of Ferris and Merrifield.

headline: Medora rising across the river
summary: Roosevelt is at the Pyramid Park Hotel in Little Missouri. Across the river the French Marquis de Mores has been building Medora since April, named for his wife, with grand plans to ship beef east in refrigerated rail cars.

events.detail: Stays at the Pyramid Park Hotel
The Marquis de Mores is building the new town of Medora across the river

uncertain: The record says only that Roosevelt probably saw Medora being built.

headline: At the Pyramid Park Hotel
summary: Roosevelt remains at the Pyramid Park Hotel in Little Missouri.

headline: Trophy work in Bismarck
summary: In Bismarck, Roosevelt arranges to have his bison head mounted.

events.detail: Arranges for the bison head to be mounted

headline: Back in Little Missouri
summary: Roosevelt is in Little Missouri.

headline: Ranch partnership made final
summary: With Ferris and Merrifield back, Roosevelt's first contract with them is completed. It is also his sister Conie's 22nd birthday.

events.detail: Finalizes his first ranch contract with Ferris and Merrifield

uncertain: The record says the partners returned from Montana, though its September 19 entry sends them to Minnesota.

headline: Heading home; partners go for cattle
summary: Roosevelt starts back to New York while Ferris and Merrifield travel to Iowa to buy 300 head of cattle.

events.detail: Leaves Dakota for New York City
Ferris and Merrifield go to Iowa to purchase 300 cattle

headline: On the train east
summary: Roosevelt is traveling back to New York City.

headline: Family doubts about the Dakota venture
summary: Roosevelt is still traveling east. Mittie writes a friend that Alice's pregnancy is now plainly showing. The family, above all Uncle James Roosevelt, head of Roosevelt and Son, frowns on Roosevelt's Badlands investment.

events.detail: Mittie writes Mrs. Hilborne West about Alice's advancing pregnancy
Uncle James Roosevelt and others disapprove of his Badlands investment

uncertain: The record spells 'Hilbourne'. This James Roosevelt is TR's uncle, not FDR's father.

summary: Roosevelt continues his trip to New York City.

events.detail: En route to New York City

events.detail: Re-elected to the Assembly over Wallace Bamberg by 1,200 votes
Watches returns at Republican headquarters as his party takes both houses

events.detail: Goes to Albany and stays at the Delavan Hotel
Lobbies members for the Speakership with John J. O'Brien's backing

headline: Speakership slips away to Titus Sheard
summary: The Republican caucus picks Titus Sheard, not Roosevelt, for Speaker. Members break pledges as machine men and corporate lobbyists close ranks, and Senator Miller wins over John O'Brien. Stung, Roosevelt moves to make Sheard's nomination unanimous. His year-end notes also tally his Dakota game and his 1883 income.

events.detail: Loses the caucus Speakership nomination to Titus Sheard
Moves that the caucus unanimously back Sheard
Records his Little Missouri game tally and the guns he used, including a shotgun from Elliott
Accounts for 1883 income, about $13,920, including $1,200 from the Legislature

uncertain: The game list and account ledger are hard to read in the record and are not quoted. The ledger notes $350 of legislative pay stolen and a cut-off line about an Oyster Bay lodge or stable.
